correctness.rationale: In branch mass coordinates for A_1 through A_(n−1), column 1 of the open transfer matrix consists of a_j, and column j>1 shifts mass to j−1. This verifies the finite Perron polynomial directly: λm_j=a_j m_1+m_(j+1), with m_n=0, implies Σa_j λ^(−j)=1. The root above 1 in z=1/λ is unique; summation by parts gives S_n=Σk^(−θ)−n^(1−θ), with the sum up to n. With δ=θ−1 the integral I=log(n) Ψ(δ log n) diverges for δ→0, and e^(−c)/I≤|δ|+1/log n for either sign (by e^v−1≥v). Thus S_n/I→1 and nγ≤e^(−c)/S_n→0. The power-series remainder relative to γ S_n is bounded by nγ exp(nγ)/2, proving the leading result without bounded c. For bounded c, subtract the integral from the sum cell by cell: the discrepancy series is locally differentiable at δ=0 with summable derivative, so S_n=log(n) Ψ(c)+γ_E−e^(−c)+O_C(1/log n). The exact second moment is O_C(n) by a_k≤θk^(−θ−1), giving relative exponential remainder O_C((log n)^(−2)). This establishes the stated coefficient, error and continuous c=0 limit. The proof concerns the finite branch spectral rate, not arbitrary survivor distributions.
residual_risks: The Euler correction is uniform only for bounded c. The −e^(−c) term depends on retaining exactly branches 1 to n−1.

evidence: The harmonic denominator H_n−1 in Knight–Munday already contains γ_E−1 at c=0; fixed-θ estimates do not resolve unbounded c_n.
Example 3.3 claims γ̃=Z(−log Z)/Σk p_k. For N≥2, strict Jensen gives log E_{p/Z} exp(kγ)>γ E_{p/Z}k, hence γ̃>γ for the root. For θ=1,n=3, γ=log[(√33−3)/2], whereas γ̃=(4/5)log(3/2).
γ̃=t_n/S_n [1+O(t_n)], so it has the same coefficients; the independently justified γ=t_n/S_n [1+O_C((log n)^(−2))] in the bounded window is what transfers those coefficients to the correct root.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct result is the joint, all-sequences leading equivalent and the uniform bounded-window first correction for the true finite-matrix spectral root. Knight–Munday already give the root equation, the fixed-parameter asymptotics and the harmonic denominator at θ=1; those are not credited. The strongest apparent coverage, Bonanno–Tikekar's claimed exact induced-to-original rate formula instantiated on the identical branch model, is not an identity for that root. It gives the same near-critical coefficients as an approximation, but transferring those to the actual root requires accuracy estimates not provided by that exact identity. Thus no verified prior implication supplies the moving-parameter result.
residual_risks: The earlier induced expression shares the same expansion when used as an approximation. Priority for a correct uniform transfer of that approximation to the spectral root remains subject to uncataloged literature.

value.rationale: The finite/infinite invariant-measure boundary makes this joint limit natural. It quantifies the failure of interpolating the two fixed-parameter limits, gives relative control even when the scaled rate vanishes or diverges, and distinguishes the finite-hole correction from a mere replacement of the harmonic series by an integral. The proof provides accuracy control for the actual clock-time spectral observable, not just the induced rate divided by mean return time.
residual_risks: The value is the moving-threshold spectral theorem for a canonical Markov-hole family, not a statement about non-Markov holes or all initial laws.
